A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same FOREVER study. Their main text, equations, figures, tables and complete appendices are readable and matchable despite additions and renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original continual-learning experiments across three benchmarks and multiple backbones, with component ablations and additional appendix analyses.

after.justification: v2 retains those original experiments and adds replay-scheduling comparisons, full-parameter fine-tuning, forgetting measurements, longer task sequences and correlation analyses.

M1.justification: The parameter-update clock, replay scheduler, intensity-dependent regularization and objectives remain unchanged. Algorithm 1's replay-epoch correction aligns its pseudocode with the two-epoch default already documented in v1; it does not establish a redesigned method.

E1.justification: Appendix B.8 adds a jointly evaluated, shuffled 30-task stream combining Long Sequence and SuperNI. This extends evaluation to a longer mixed-task scenario while retaining the underlying datasets and task collections.

E2.justification: Section 3.4 and Table 3 add exponential and polynomial replay schedules as evaluated alternatives. The external baseline membership in Table 1 and the original component comparisons in Table 2 remain unchanged.

E3.justification: v2 adds comparisons controlling replay budgets and cumulative replayed data, full-parameter fine-tuning, and a shuffled 30-task sequence. It also introduces old-task loss measurements over five 60-step intervals and extends the warm-up sweep with S values of 3, 6 and 96. These substantially expand the evaluation design.

E4.justification: New analyses test whether increasing spacing matters under matched replay budgets, whether forgetting actually slows during training, and whether model-day calibration relates to task order, difficulty and final forgetting. Appendix B.7 extends the existing warm-up sensitivity analysis; its intermediate values repeat retained results rather than constitute entirely new evidence.

E5.justification: Appendix C introduces Pearson correlations and p-values for task-order consistency, final BWT and task difficulty, including r = 0.7379 and p = 0.0017 for order consistency. Both versions already report averaging experiments over three independent runs; no increase in run counts is established.

E6.justification: Existing benchmark and ablation values are retained, while Tables 3, 4 and 9–11 and Appendix C add substantial results. Examples include FOREVER's OP/BWT of 47.5/-2.2 under full-parameter fine-tuning and 27.9/-10.8 in the 30-task setting. These are newly evaluated conditions, not same-setting performance changes between versions.

T1.justification: The mathematical formulation, model-time definitions and objectives remain unchanged, with no added theorem, proof or substantive derivation. The new loss-per-step statistic is a standard empirical rate calculation used in the added evaluation.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's contributions and conclusion retain the same central claims: model-update dynamics determine replay timing and strength, improving continual learning across three benchmarks and backbones spanning 0.6B–13B parameters. The new experiments support these claims without rewriting their core scope.

C2.justification: v2 substantially expands its interpretation of increasing spacing as a structural principle and explicitly disclaims biological equivalence. It newly interprets calibration as applicable beyond LoRA, explains extreme warm-up settings, and distinguishes task-local parameter drift from final cross-task forgetting. The original limitations remain.

D1.justification: The code-access reference changes from an anonymous 4open.science repository to WoodScene/FOREVER on GitHub. Algorithm 1, line 18, changes one replay epoch to two, resolving its inconsistency with the existing implementation details and replay-epoch study. The main hardware, hyperparameters and decoding details are retained.

R1.justification: The cited works and related-work discussion are unchanged. The positioning relative to regularization, architectural adaptation, replay methods and cognitive forgetting research is retained.

P1.justification: v2 adds Section 3.4 and several appendix subsections while preserving the existing narrative and nearly all original prose. Appendix references are updated, and one author affiliation changes from AI Technology Center of OVB to Solar System of OVB.

P2.justification: Five new tables present controlled scheduling, full-parameter fine-tuning, forgetting rates, extended warm-up sensitivity and 30-task results, substantially expanding the displayed empirical evidence. Figures 1–7 are retained. Existing appendix tables and figures are relocated, and Algorithm 1 now shares a page with the task-order table.

improvement.justification: The matched-budget comparisons and direct forgetting measurements strengthen v1's scheduling rationale, while additional training-setting checks and the replay-epoch correction improve validation and consistency. The gains remain bounded: most new analyses use Qwen3-0.6B on SuperNI, and Section 3.4's claim that the standard schedule performs best needs qualification because Table 3 gives the exponential schedule better BWT. Overall, v2 provides useful additional support with some overinterpretation.
